dominionBloodedSpears.name: Blooded Spears
dominionBloodedSpears.flavor: First blood is the cheapest lesson the wild ever sells.
dominionBloodedSpears.text: Military units gain +2 strength, doubled against barbarians.

paymasters.name: Paymasters
paymasters.flavor: Two clerks, one strongbox, and an army that turns up on time.
paymasters.text: Barracks give +3 gold. Each garrisoned unit costs 1 less upkeep, minimum zero.

musterRites.name: Muster Rites
musterRites.flavor: A sword blessed, a bowl filled, a name on the roll.
musterRites.text: Gaining a unit grants 8 faith and 8 food.

theWarChronicle.name: The War Chronicle
theWarChronicle.flavor: Every victory is written down, and the writing is worth something.
theWarChronicle.text: While slotted, pays +3 science and +3 culture, and gains +3 of each for every enemy unit you kill.

dominionConscription.name: Conscription
dominionConscription.flavor: The levy takes the sons and leaves the ledger short.
dominionConscription.text: +20% production toward units. Cities producing a unit lose 2 gold.

pathfinders.name: Pathfinders
pathfinders.flavor: They know the country before the country knows them.

dominionTheStandingArmy.name: The Standing Army
dominionTheStandingArmy.flavor: Not raised for a war. Simply raised.
dominionTheStandingArmy.text: Garrisoned units cost no upkeep. Cities with a Barracks gain +30% production toward military units.

bloodBrothers.name: Blood Brothers
bloodBrothers.flavor: Beaten once, fed twice, and loyal ever after.
bloodBrothers.text: A barbarian unit you kill joins your side.

theKingsLevy.name: The King's Levy
theKingsLevy.flavor: The king remembers the villages, and the villages remember the king.
theKingsLevy.text: Every fifteen turns your capital raises a melee unit for free. It costs no upkeep.

dominionClearTheFrontier.name: Commission: Clear the Frontier
dominionClearTheFrontier.flavor: A young state wins its first war against the camps at its edge.
dominionClearTheFrontier.text: Commission. Clear two barbarian camps while this card is seated. Then gain 60 production in your capital and the best melee unit you can build is trained in your capital, free of upkeep. The card leaves its chair.

dominionTheHorseHerds.name: The Horse Herds
dominionTheHorseHerds.flavor: The herd is counted before the harvest.
dominionTheHorseHerds.text: Worked pastures and camps give +1 food and +1 production.

dominionBattleHonours.name: Battle Honours
dominionBattleHonours.flavor: The names go on the standard, one by one.
dominionBattleHonours.text: Commission. Kill ten units while this card is seated. Then choose a great general from a draft. The card leaves its chair.

dominionSwordAndPlough.name: Sword and Plough
dominionSwordAndPlough.flavor: The same hands hold both, one season at a time.
dominionSwordAndPlough.text: Each city with a garrison gains +1 culture and +2 production.

dominionTheCampChaplains.name: The Camp Chaplains
dominionTheCampChaplains.flavor: Every tent has a prayer said over it.
dominionTheCampChaplains.text: Killing a unit grants faith equal to its strength.

theGrainTribute.name: The Grain Tribute
theGrainTribute.flavor: The villages feed the army that guards them.
theGrainTribute.text: +1 food and +1 production in every city.

theScalingLadders.name: The Scaling Ladders
theScalingLadders.flavor: A wall is only as tall as the longest ladder.
theScalingLadders.text: Melee units gain +4 strength against towns.

theFuneralGames.name: The Funeral Games
theFuneralGames.flavor: The games are held for the dead, and the living come to watch.
theFuneralGames.text: When one of your units falls, gain faith equal to its strength.

theBardsPraise.name: The Bards' Praise
theBardsPraise.flavor: Every fight becomes a song, and every song finds a crowd.
theBardsPraise.text: Killing a unit grants culture equal to its strength. Clearing a barbarian camp grants 15 culture.

theCattleRaid.name: The Cattle Raid
theCattleRaid.flavor: Burn the camp, and drive its cattle home.
theCattleRaid.text: Clearing a barbarian camp gives every city +3 food for ten turns. Clearing another restarts the ten turns.

theDrillGrounds.name: The Drill Grounds
theDrillGrounds.flavor: Every fourth morning, the whole garrison drills in the square.
theDrillGrounds.text: Units standing in your towns gain 1 experience every 4 turns.

theArmedColony.name: The Armed Colony
theArmedColony.flavor: The soldiers marked out the walls before the farmers marked out the fields.
theArmedColony.text: A town founded beside one of your military units starts with three extra hexes, and that unit becomes a Veteran.

theCampaignAnnals.name: The Campaign Annals
theCampaignAnnals.flavor: Every promotion is written down, with the battle that earned it.
theCampaignAnnals.text: While seated, this card gains +1 science each time one of your units earns a rank. It starts at +3 science.

theOutriders.name: The Outriders
theOutriders.flavor: The scouts ride ahead, and every town hears what they found.
theOutriders.text: Claiming a discovery or clearing a barbarian camp grants 8 production to every town.

theGarrisonCaptains.name: The Garrison Captains
theGarrisonCaptains.flavor: A captain in every town, and every captain answers to the throne.

theCapturedArms.name: The Captured Arms
theCapturedArms.flavor: Every blade taken from the field is studied before it is melted down.
theCapturedArms.text: +1 science for every unit you have killed this game, no cap.

drillManuals.name: The Training Cadre
drillManuals.flavor: The recruits arrive already knowing how to stand in line.
drillManuals.text: Units gained in a town with a Barracks start with 2 experience.

dominionMarchDiscipline.name: The Marching Camps
dominionMarchDiscipline.flavor: Every night the legion digs a camp, and every morning it fights from one.
dominionMarchDiscipline.text: Attacking does not break your units' fortification.

dominionFieldSurgeons.name: Field Surgeons
dominionFieldSurgeons.flavor: Dug in and stitched up, in that order.
dominionFieldSurgeons.text: Military units heal an extra 10 health while fortified.

dominionTheQuartermasters.name: The Quartermasters
dominionTheQuartermasters.flavor: The iron and the horses are counted before the men are.
dominionTheQuartermasters.text: Worked strategic resources gain +3 food and +3 production.

victorySteles.name: Victory Steles
victorySteles.flavor: Stone remembers what the treasury forgets.
victorySteles.text: Gain +1 authority capacity for every two Monuments you hold. Monuments give +2 production.

huntersOfferings.name: Hunters' Offerings
huntersOfferings.flavor: The first of the catch goes to the fire.
huntersOfferings.text: Worked fishing boats, camps and pastures gain +1 production and +1 faith.

quarryLevies.name: Quarry Levies
quarryLevies.flavor: The hill pays in stone and the stone pays in coin.
quarryLevies.text: Worked mines and quarries gain +1 production and +1 gold.

ritesOfArms.name: Rites of Arms
ritesOfArms.flavor: Bless the spear, then make another.
ritesOfArms.text: Cities keeping a rite gain +2 production and +20% production toward units.

theSoldiersPurse.name: The Soldiers' Purse
theSoldiersPurse.flavor: A soldier who feeds himself costs the crown less.
theSoldiersPurse.text: Military units cost 1 less upkeep for each rank they hold.

veteransRest.name: Veterans' Rest
veteransRest.flavor: The old sergeants keep the peace by standing in it.
veteransRest.text: Cities with a Barracks or a War Hall gain +1 happiness, and +1 more per garrisoned unit.
deferred: a town with a barracks or a war hall is gladder, and gladder still for each unit standing in it

theWarHallSchools.name: Honours of the Legion
theWarHallSchools.flavor: Each new honour is read out in front of the whole legion.
theWarHallSchools.text: Each time one of your units earns a rank, gain science and culture equal to its strength.

shorePatrols.name: Shore Patrols
shorePatrols.flavor: The nets are safer when somebody is watching the water.
shorePatrols.text: Worked fishing boats gain +1 production. Coastal cities with a Harbour gain +1 happiness.

dominionTheMarshals.name: The Marshals
dominionTheMarshals.flavor: Nobody in the line is alone, and the enemy can count.
dominionTheMarshals.text: +2 strength per adjacent friendly combat unit, at most +6.

foragersRight.name: Foragers' Right
foragersRight.flavor: The garrison eats from the country it guards.
foragersRight.text: Per garrisoned unit, the city's worked resource tiles gain +1 food and +1 production.
deferred: every unit standing in a town makes that town’s worked resource tiles pay more grain and more hammers

theWarlordsCall.name: The Warlord's Call
theWarlordsCall.flavor: One name is enough to raise a war.
theWarlordsCall.text: On first activation only, grants a great general. Citadels gain +3 food and +3 production while this card is active.
deferred: the first time this is seated a great general answers the call, once and never again
citadels pay more grain and more hammers while it sits in a chair

armyContracts.name: Army Contracts
armyContracts.flavor: The barracks orders, the road delivers.
armyContracts.text: Routes from a city with a Barracks or a Stable gain +2 gold and +1 production; +4 gold and +2 production with both.
armyContracts.note: Two lines, one for each hall: a town that keeps both sends its caravans out under both.

dominionTheMusterRolls.name: The Muster Rolls
dominionTheMusterRolls.flavor: Each name written is a coin of knowledge.
dominionTheMusterRolls.text: While slotted, gains +1 science and +1 culture each time you train a unit. Purchases do not count.

thePacifiedMarches.name: The Pacified Marches
thePacifiedMarches.flavor: A burnt camp is a quiet border.
thePacifiedMarches.text: Gains +1 authority capacity and +5 culture for every barbarian camp cleared this game, at most +8 authority and +40 culture.

theArtOfWar.name: The Art of War
theArtOfWar.flavor: Every sword teaches the smith something.
theArtOfWar.text: Gaining a unit grants science equal to three quarters of its strength.

soldierSettlers.name: Soldier-Settlers
soldierSettlers.flavor: Spear in one hand, spade in the other.
soldierSettlers.text: Newly founded cities receive a free melee unit. Newly trained melee units carry one builder charge, for improvements or a chop.
deferred: a town you found comes with a melee unit already standing in it
a melee unit you train can do a worker’s job once, building an improvement or felling a wood

theSeaLevy.name: The Sea Levy
theSeaLevy.flavor: The fleet is a village that floats.
theSeaLevy.text: Ships cost 1 less upkeep. Training a naval unit grants culture equal to its strength.
deferred: ships are cheaper to keep
training a ship pays culture in proportion to how strong that ship is
theSeaLevy.note: Half built and therefore not built: training a hull may now pay for how strong it is, but a payroll is discounted as a share of the whole army and cannot be forgiven a coin at a time for one kind of piece.

warFoundries.name: War Foundries
warFoundries.flavor: The forges run whether the war does or not.
warFoundries.text: Cities with a Barracks gain gold equal to 30% of their base production and +38% production toward military units.

songsOfTheFallen.name: Songs of the Fallen
songsOfTheFallen.flavor: We lose them twice: once in the field, once in the song.
songsOfTheFallen.text: Killing or losing a unit grants science and culture equal to twice its strength.

universalConscription.name: Universal Conscription
universalConscription.flavor: Every man, every year, and no more hired swords.
universalConscription.text: +50% production toward units. Once slotted, you may never purchase a unit again this game.
deferred: your cities put much more production behind units
once this has been seated you may never buy a unit again for the rest of the game, even after it leaves the chair

dominionHorseLords.name: Horse Lords
dominionHorseLords.flavor: They were born in the saddle and see no reason to leave it.
dominionHorseLords.text: Mounted units gain +3 strength and +1 movement.

dominionTheGeneralStaff.name: The General Staff
dominionTheGeneralStaff.flavor: The maps are kept here, and so are the men who read them.
dominionTheGeneralStaff.text: Cities with a Barracks give +3 production and +2 renown a turn, favouring great generals.

dominionTheSoldierFarmers.name: The Soldier-Farmers
dominionTheSoldierFarmers.flavor: In spring they drill, in summer they reap.
dominionTheSoldierFarmers.text: While at peace, garrisoned cities gain +2 food and +2 production on each worked pasture and camp.

martialLaw.name: Martial Law
martialLaw.flavor: The garrison eats first, and the town sleeps sound for it.
martialLaw.text: Each garrisoned unit grants its city +2 happiness and +4 food.

walledTowns.name: Walled Towns
walledTowns.flavor: Inside the walls, a farmer plants without looking over his shoulder.
walledTowns.text: Towns with a defensive building, such as a Palisade or walls, gain +15% food.

theSwiftRiders.name: The Swift Riders
theSwiftRiders.flavor: Strike, wheel away, and strike again somewhere else.
theSwiftRiders.text: Mounted units may move after attacking.

theCaptiveCraftsmen.name: The Captive Craftsmen
theCaptiveCraftsmen.flavor: The smiths came home with the army, though not by choice.
theCaptiveCraftsmen.text: Gains +1 science and +1 production each time you pillage a hex.

theSatraps.name: The Satraps
theSatraps.flavor: The governor rules the province, and the garrison makes sure of it.
theSatraps.text: Garrisoned towns in unrest pacify twice as fast.

theAcropolis.name: The Acropolis
theAcropolis.flavor: The high city holds the temples, the treasury and the will of the state.
theAcropolis.text: +1 authority for each building in your capital.

siegeWorks.name: Siege Works
siegeWorks.flavor: Walls are patient. The engines are not.
siegeWorks.text: +38% production toward siege units. Siege units gain +4 strength against cities.

dominionTheWarChest.name: The War Chest
dominionTheWarChest.flavor: Kept locked, kept counted, kept full.
dominionTheWarChest.text: Military units cost 1 less upkeep, minimum zero. Barracks give +3 gold.

armouryGuilds.name: Armoury Guilds
armouryGuilds.flavor: The smiths keep books as carefully as they keep fires.
armouryGuilds.text: When one of your units falls, your nearest town with an Armoury gains production equal to its strength.

veteransBoroughs.name: Veterans' Boroughs
veteransBoroughs.flavor: A quarter of the city where everyone has served.
veteransBoroughs.text: Cities of at least ten population with an Armoury gain +3 happiness and +20% science.

conqueredArchives.name: Conquered Archives
conqueredArchives.flavor: Their records are ours now, and they were good records.
conqueredArchives.text: Captured cities gain +6 science and +6 culture.

stockpiles.name: Stockpiles
stockpiles.flavor: Walls are no use to a hungry town.
stockpiles.text: Cities gain +8 food per defensive building.

thePostRoads.name: The Post Roads
thePostRoads.flavor: News travels, and so does bread.
thePostRoads.text: Cities connected by road gain +1 happiness and +2 production.

provincialGarrisons.name: Provincial Garrisons
provincialGarrisons.flavor: The soldiers build when they are not fighting.
provincialGarrisons.text: Per garrisoned unit, the city gains +10% production toward buildings.
deferred: every unit standing in a town puts more of that town’s production behind its buildings

dominionTriumphs.name: Triumphs
dominionTriumphs.flavor: They will speak of the day the gates opened.
dominionTriumphs.text: Capturing a city grants culture equal to fifteen times its population.

dominionCampFollowers.name: Camp Followers
dominionCampFollowers.flavor: Where the armoury is, the wagons gather.
dominionCampFollowers.text: Cities with an Armoury gain +3 food and +3 gold.

navalYards.name: Naval Yards
navalYards.flavor: Timber, tar, and a town that smells of both.
navalYards.text: Cities with a Shipyard gain +10% production and +2 culture. Ships trained there gain +10 health.

dominionScorchedEarth.name: Scorched Earth
dominionScorchedEarth.flavor: The smoke is an offering, and somebody is counting it.
dominionScorchedEarth.text: Pillaging heals the acting unit by 20 and pays the hex's gold yield again in faith.
deferred: the unit that burns a tile mends
the coin that tile would have paid is paid to you again as faith

marineDrill.name: Marine Drill
marineDrill.flavor: The men who come off the boats come off them running.
marineDrill.text: Naval melee units gain +4 strength. Land units attacking on the turn they disembark gain +3 strength.
marineDrill.note: The blessing is hung on the piece the moment it wades ashore, and lasts the turn it landed.

dominionRidersOfTheSteppe.name: Riders of the Steppe
dominionRidersOfTheSteppe.flavor: They burn the farm without slowing to a walk.
dominionRidersOfTheSteppe.text: Mounted units ignore enemy zone of control. Pillaging costs them one less movement point, minimum zero.
dominionRidersOfTheSteppe.note: A raid costs a single point of movement, so a rider who is forgiven one is forgiven the raid.

fortifications.name: Fortifications
fortifications.flavor: A ditch, a bank, a night's work, a year's safety.
fortifications.text: Workers may build forts on open ground without forest or jungle. A fort gives +2 food and +2 production, and friendly units fortified on it gain +5 strength.
deferred: your workers may throw up a fort on open ground
a fort pays grain and hammers, and a unit dug in on one fights harder

beachheads.name: Beachheads
beachheads.flavor: The water is a road if you are quick about it.
beachheads.text: Embarking and disembarking cost no movement.
deferred: taking to the water costs your units no movement, and so does coming ashore

theLongMarch.name: The Long March
theLongMarch.flavor: The infantry arrive first and complain longest.
theLongMarch.text: Melee units gain +1 strength and +1 movement.

theIronLevy.name: The Iron Levy
theIronLevy.flavor: Iron makes soldiers cheap and everything else dear.
theIronLevy.text: +1 production toward units per strategic resource you hold, at most +6. Units cost 1 less upkeep while you hold iron.
deferred: each strategic resource you hold puts a little more production behind every unit, up to a limit
while you hold iron, units are cheaper to keep

undermining.name: Undermining
undermining.flavor: Walls stand on ground, and ground can be moved.
undermining.text: Your units gain +8 strength against cities with walls. Siege units ignore zone of control.
deferred: your units fight harder against a city that has walls
siege engines walk past an enemy picket for nothing

mercenaryCompanies.name: Mercenary Companies
mercenaryCompanies.flavor: Loyalty by the season, paid in advance.
mercenaryCompanies.text: Military units cost 25% less gold to purchase in cities with a Barracks. A purchased unit arrives with +10 health.

leviesOfTheProvinces.name: Levies of the Provinces
leviesOfTheProvinces.flavor: The new subjects are drilled before they are trusted.
leviesOfTheProvinces.text: Captured cities produce units 30% faster and gain +2 food.

spoilsOfWar.name: Spoils of War
spoilsOfWar.flavor: The wagons come home heavier than they went.
spoilsOfWar.text: Pillaging grants 15 production to your city nearest the pillaged hex. The first pillage each turn also grants 30 culture.

warlords.name: Warlords
warlords.flavor: Each of them thinks the army is his.
warlords.text: Each great general you hold gives +10% production toward units. Citadels gain +2 production and +2 culture.
deferred: every great general you have earned puts more production behind your units
citadels pay hammers and culture
warlords.note: Held whole. Hammers behind a thing can be counted off what the realm holds now, but the great people it holds are not among the things it can count.

prizeCourts.name: Prize Courts
prizeCourts.flavor: The lawyers follow the fleet and take their share.
prizeCourts.text: Capturing a coastal city grants gold equal to twenty times its population. Ships adjacent to a city you capture heal fully.
deferred: taking a coastal city pays gold in proportion to how many people lived in it
your ships beside a city you take are mended completely
prizeCourts.note: Half built and therefore not built: a capture may now pay for the people who lived in the town, but nothing tells a coastal town from an inland one at that moment, and a payout mends the whole army or none of it — never the hulls standing beside the gate.

theAdmiralty.name: The Admiralty
theAdmiralty.flavor: Charts, contracts and a room full of arguments.
theAdmiralty.text: +1 trade-route capacity per two Shipyards, at most +2. Naval units gain +1 sight.

blockade.name: Blockade
blockade.flavor: Nothing goes in. That is the whole of the plan.
blockade.text: A hostile coastal city with one of your ships adjacent counts as besieged. Routes into it are plundered at your ship.
deferred: one of your ships beside an enemy coastal city puts that city under siege
a caravan bound for it is plundered where your ship sits

dominionHegemony.name: Hegemony
dominionHegemony.flavor: They keep their walls. We keep the keys.
dominionHegemony.text: Captured cities you hold cost one less authority. Capturing a city grants +30% production in every city for ten turns.

triumphalReturn.name: Triumphal Return
triumphalReturn.flavor: The marvel is ours now, and the men feel it.
triumphalReturn.text: Capturing a city that holds a wonder heals all your units.

theBloodLedger.name: The Blood Ledger
theBloodLedger.flavor: Every name in it is worth twice what it was.
theBloodLedger.text: The yields from killing or losing a unit are doubled.
deferred: everything you are paid for killing a unit, or for losing one, is paid twice over — the one-off rewards and the standing ones alike
theBloodLedger.note: Not built: a card may scale what an occasion pays out of itself, and a kill pays nothing out of itself — everything it hands over is another card's grant. Doubling one card's gifts from a second card is a reading nothing in the vocabulary makes, and the standing counters the text also names are not payouts at all.

masterBowyers.name: Master Bowyers
masterBowyers.flavor: A longer arm wins more arguments.
masterBowyers.text: Ranged and siege units gain +1 range.

dominionPaxImperia.name: Pax Imperia
dominionPaxImperia.flavor: The peace is ours, and it is profitable.
dominionPaxImperia.text: While at peace, every city gains +20% production and +2 happiness. Declaring war silences this card for twenty turns.
deferred: while you are at peace every city makes more and is gladder
declaring war silences this card for a long stretch of turns

theSeaTreasury.name: The Sea Treasury
theSeaTreasury.flavor: The harbour guard is paid out of the harbour.
theSeaTreasury.text: Per garrisoned unit, a coastal city gains production equal to 25% of its gold yield.
deferred: every unit standing in a coastal town turns part of that town’s coin into hammers

dominionTheCitadelWorks.name: The Citadel Works
dominionTheCitadelWorks.flavor: Each fortress keeps a library of its own sieges.
dominionTheCitadelWorks.text: Citadels gain +5 science. Each citadel inside your borders gives +1 renown a turn, favouring great generals.

dominionTheRelayStations.name: The Relay Stations
dominionTheRelayStations.flavor: Fresh horses wait at every post.
dominionTheRelayStations.text: Once a turn, a military unit that starts its turn in a city connected to your capital may move to any other connected city, ending its move there.
deferred: Moving a unit from one connected city to another in a single order needs a new order on the map, which the game does not have yet.

dominionWarReparations.name: War Reparations
dominionWarReparations.flavor: The loser pays, and the winner counts it twice.
dominionWarReparations.text: Making peace after taking cities in that war grants gold equal to twenty times their total population, and half as much culture.
deferred: The game does not yet pay anything when a peace is signed, or remember which cities each side took during a war.

dominionTakeTheCity.name: Commission: Take the City
dominionTakeTheCity.flavor: One city taken is a lesson for the rest.
dominionTakeTheCity.text: Commission. Capture a city with at least five citizens. Then gain culture and science equal to twenty-three times its population, and a free Barracks in that city. The card leaves its chair.

theValetudinaria.name: The Valetudinaria
theValetudinaria.flavor: A soldier mended at home is a soldier who marches again.
theValetudinaria.text: Units in your territory heal 15 more hit points a turn.

livingOffTheLand.name: Living off the Land
livingOffTheLand.flavor: The army eats what it finds.
livingOffTheLand.text: Military units outside your territory cost no upkeep.

theSerriedRanks.name: The Serried Ranks
theSerriedRanks.flavor: Shoulder to shoulder, the line does not break.
theSerriedRanks.text: Melee units beside another melee unit gain +10 strength when defending.

theConscriptionRolls.name: The Conscription Rolls
theConscriptionRolls.flavor: Every large town owes the army its share of men.
theConscriptionRolls.text: Every ten turns, each town of at least eight citizens raises the best melee unit you can build.

theVeteransRoll.name: The Veterans' Roll
theVeteransRoll.flavor: Every name on the roll has served, and the roll grows longer every year.
theVeteransRoll.text: +1% science and culture for every rank your units have earned this game, at most +30%.

theTactica.name: The Tactica
theTactica.flavor: The manual says where every officer should stand, and why.
theTactica.text: At the end of your turn, great generals give 1 experience to every unit beside them. Each time one of your units earns a rank, gain 15 science.

theFabricae.name: The Fabricae
theFabricae.flavor: The old soldiers know what a good blade is worth, and the smiths listen.
theFabricae.text: Towns whose garrison is a Veteran or Elite gain +25% production.

theSagas.name: The Sagas
theSagas.flavor: Every burnt farmstead became a verse.
theSagas.text: +1% culture and gold for every three hexes you have pillaged this game, at most +30%.

theHallOfTheSlain.name: The Hall of the Slain
theHallOfTheSlain.flavor: Every name on the wall is a reason to keep fighting.
theHallOfTheSlain.text: +1% production and culture for every two units you have lost this game, at most +30%.

theProvincialCensus.name: The Provincial Census
theProvincialCensus.flavor: Count the people, and you know what the province can give.
theProvincialCensus.text: Pacifying a town grants science equal to twenty times its population.

spearWonLand.name: Spear-won Land
spearWonLand.flavor: Land taken by the spear is held by the spear.
spearWonLand.text: +3% production and science for every town you have captured this game, at most +30%.

standingGarrisons.name: Standing Garrisons
standingGarrisons.flavor: The soldiers have been here so long they are townsfolk.
standingGarrisons.text: Per garrisoned unit, the city gains +12% production and +12% culture.

spoilsOfEmpire.name: Spoils of Empire
spoilsOfEmpire.text: Captured cities gain +25% gold and +25% science. Cities with a Courthouse gain +4 happiness.

theMilitaryRoads.name: The Military Roads
theMilitaryRoads.flavor: Built for grain, kept for armies.
theMilitaryRoads.text: Your military units pay nothing for a road step inside your territory. Cities connected to your capital gain +10% production.
deferred: your military units walk your own roads for nothing inside your borders
a town joined to your capital makes more

arsenals.name: Arsenals
arsenals.flavor: One yard, every weapon, all year.
arsenals.text: Cities with an Armoury gain +30% production and produce ships 75% faster.

dominionTheSiegeTrain.name: The Siege Train
dominionTheSiegeTrain.flavor: The engines go ahead, and the infantry follow the ruts.
dominionTheSiegeTrain.text: Siege units gain +1 movement. Adjacent friendly land melee units gain +6 strength against cities.

reserveOfficers.name: Reserve Officers
reserveOfficers.flavor: In peace they build. In war they do not.
reserveOfficers.text: While at war, cities with a Barracks produce military units 60% faster; while at peace, those cities gain +30% production toward buildings.

blockadeAdmirals.name: Blockade Admirals
blockadeAdmirals.flavor: They know which harbours to sit outside of.
blockadeAdmirals.text: Naval combat units gain +1 movement and +3 strength within two hexes of a hostile coastal city.
deferred: your warships move further and fight harder when they are close to an enemy coastal city

defensiveLines.name: Defensive Lines
defensiveLines.flavor: The country itself is fortified now.
defensiveLines.text: Land combat units gain +3 strength beside a friendly city. Cities with walls gain +3 defence per garrisoned unit.

warColleges.name: War Colleges
warColleges.flavor: They graduate knowing the ground and the drill.
warColleges.text: Units trained in a city with an Armoury gain +1 movement and +20 health.
deferred: a unit raised in a town with an armoury is born quicker and hardier, and stays so for life

theGrandLevy.name: The Grand Levy
theGrandLevy.flavor: Every hand in the town has a use.
theGrandLevy.text: Cities with a Barracks produce units 50% faster and gain +1 production per two citizens.

navalSupremacy.name: Naval Supremacy
navalSupremacy.flavor: The sea is a province, and we hold it.
navalSupremacy.text: Naval units gain +1 sight and +1 range. Coastal cities gain +30% gold; coastal captured cities +60%.
navalSupremacy.note: The second share is paid only where both are true, so a coastal town taken in war keeps both lines.

theLongPeace.name: The Long Peace
theLongPeace.flavor: The army waits, and costs nothing while it waits.
theLongPeace.text: While at peace, garrisoned units cost no upkeep and cities with a Barracks gain +25% culture.

theVeteransGrant.name: The Veterans' Grant
theVeteransGrant.flavor: The old soldiers came home and went to work.
theVeteransGrant.text: Each military unit you have ever trained gives your capital +2 production and +2 science, at most +60 each.
deferred: every military unit you have ever trained pays your capital hammers and beakers, up to a limit

dominionBlitz.name: Blitz
dominionBlitz.flavor: Do not stop. Stopping is how you lose a war.
dominionBlitz.text: Once per unit per turn, a combat kill restores 2 movement points. Your military units cannot fortify. This does not grant another attack.
deferred: a unit that kills gets a couple of movement points back, once a turn, and still may not strike again
your military units may not dig in
dominionBlitz.note: Not built, all three halves: the once-a-turn stamp is kept per card and this one is per piece; an occasion hands over coin, renown, a soldier or a blessing and never movement; and nothing forbids an army to dig in.

casusBelli.name: Casus Belli
casusBelli.flavor: Their capital had a name. Now it has ours.
casusBelli.text: Capturing an original capital grants a bead.
deferred: taking an empire’s first city hands you a bead of the great work

totalWar.name: Total War
totalWar.flavor: Everything is for the war. Everything.
totalWar.text: All your military units gain +5 strength and +1 movement. Every city demands +3 more happiness.

dominionAVictorsPeace.name: Commission: A Victor's Peace
dominionAVictorsPeace.flavor: A war is won at the table, after it is won in the field.
dominionAVictorsPeace.text: Commission. Make peace with an empire, or destroy it, after taking at least two of its cities in that war. Then gain 300 gold and 300 culture, and every city gains +2 happiness for twenty turns. The card leaves its chair.
deferred: The game does not yet notice a peace being signed or an empire being destroyed, or remember which cities each side took during a war.

theArriereBan.name: The Arrière-ban
theArriereBan.flavor: When the king calls the whole realm to arms, every forge answers.
theArriereBan.text: Declaring war gives every city +50% production for ten turns. Declaring war again restarts the ten turns.

theVictoryMint.name: The Victory Mint
theVictoryMint.flavor: The conquered city's silver is struck into our coins.
theVictoryMint.text: Capturing a city grants gold equal to thirty times its population.

theBoardOfOrdnance.name: The Board of Ordnance
theBoardOfOrdnance.flavor: In wartime the arsenal and the academy keep the same hours.
theBoardOfOrdnance.text: While at war, each city with a Barracks gains +1 production and +1 science for every three citizens.

theDrillMasters.name: The Drill Masters
theDrillMasters.flavor: No recruit leaves the yard until the sergeant says so.
theDrillMasters.text: Units you gain start as Veterans.

upThroughTheRanks.name: Up Through the Ranks
upThroughTheRanks.flavor: The best of them will lead armies one day.
upThroughTheRanks.text: Each time one of your units becomes an Elite, gain 250 renown, favouring great generals.

theDevshirme.name: The Devshirme
theDevshirme.flavor: Recruited in the conquered provinces, trained for years in the capital.
theDevshirme.text: Captured towns of at least six citizens may spend a citizen to raise the best melee unit you can build, as a Veteran.

theRegimentalSchools.name: The Regimental Schools
theRegimentalSchools.flavor: Between campaigns, the regiment teaches its soldiers to read.
theRegimentalSchools.text: At the end of your turn, each garrisoned unit gains 1 experience and gives its town +2 science.

theTagmata.name: The Tagmata
theTagmata.flavor: The professional regiments, kept close to the capital and paid on time.
theTagmata.text: Veteran and Elite units gain +5 strength.

theKeshik.name: The Keshik
theKeshik.flavor: The guard rides with the khan, and rides further than anyone.
theKeshik.text: Mounted Veteran and Elite units gain +1 movement.

interiorLines.name: Interior Lines
interiorLines.flavor: The army that holds the centre can reach any part of the front first.
interiorLines.text: A step along a road costs 40% less movement. A unit that has not moved this turn gains +4 strength when attacking.

thePlunderTrains.name: The Plunder Trains
thePlunderTrains.flavor: The carts went out empty and came home full.
thePlunderTrains.text: Pillaging grants 30 production and 15 food to your capital.

theYam.name: The Yam
theYam.flavor: A fresh horse waits at every post station.
theYam.text: Mounted units heal fully when they pillage.

theChevauchee.name: The Chevauchée
theChevauchee.flavor: Burn the countryside, and the towns go hungry behind their walls.
theChevauchee.text: Pillaging a hex damages enemy cities within three hexes with 50% of the pillaging unit's strength.

theBakufu.name: The Bakufu
theBakufu.flavor: The government of the tent: where the general camps, the realm is ruled.
theBakufu.text: A great general standing in a town gives it +25% science and +25% culture, and pacifies it at once.

paxRomana.name: Pax Romana
paxRomana.flavor: They make a desert and call it peace, but the roads are safe.
paxRomana.text: Towns you capture are pacified at once, and each costs 1 less authority to hold.

dominionImperium.name: Imperium
dominionImperium.flavor: The provinces pay for the great work.
dominionImperium.text: Each captured city you hold gives +10% production toward the Magnum Opus, at most +40%.

dominionHoldTheCapitals.name: Commission: Hold the Capitals
dominionHoldTheCapitals.flavor: Two thrones, and neither of them yours by birth.
dominionHoldTheCapitals.text: Commission. Hold two original capitals other than your own at the same time. Then every city gains +25% production for twenty turns, and you gain a great general. The card leaves its chair.

dominionSpolia.name: Spolia
dominionSpolia.flavor: Their columns hold up our roof now.
dominionSpolia.text: Capturing a city that was raising a Magnum Opus adds half the production it had put into that Opus to your own. If you have not begun one, the production is kept until you do.

dominionTheLegionsLabour.name: The Legions' Labour
dominionTheLegionsLabour.flavor: Between wars, the legions build walls and roads.
dominionTheLegionsLabour.text: Disbanding a military unit in a city building a wonder or the Magnum Opus adds half the unit's production cost toward it. Units raised for free add nothing.
deferred: Disbanding a unit pays nothing today, so the game cannot yet put a disbanded unit's work into a wonder.

dominionThePraetorianGuard.name: The Praetorian Guard
dominionThePraetorianGuard.flavor: The great work has its own guard, and the guard has its own walls.
dominionThePraetorianGuard.text: The city raising your Magnum Opus gains +5 defence for each unit garrisoned there. Your military units within two hexes of it gain +6 strength.

dominionTheGrandArmy.name: The Grand Army
dominionTheGrandArmy.flavor: Every regiment sends its reports to the capital.
dominionTheGrandArmy.text: Your capital gains +1 science and +1 culture for every military unit you have, at most +30 of each.

dominionTheAnnexedProvinces.name: The Annexed Provinces
dominionTheAnnexedProvinces.flavor: What they built, the whole empire now uses.
dominionTheAnnexedProvinces.text: Each captured city you hold gives +5% science and +5% culture in every city, at most +25%.

dominionTheMarshalate.name: The Marshalate
dominionTheMarshalate.flavor: Each baton was earned on a field with a name.
dominionTheMarshalate.text: Each great general you have called gives your military units +1 strength, at most +5. Citadels give +3 culture and +3 production.

dominionTheMilitaryFrontier.name: The Military Frontier
dominionTheMilitaryFrontier.flavor: Every household keeps a musket over the door.
dominionTheMilitaryFrontier.text: Each unit garrisoned in a city gives it +3 science and +3 culture, at most three units per city.

dominionTheNationInArms.name: The Nation in Arms
dominionTheNationInArms.flavor: Every armoury opens its doors on the same morning.
dominionTheNationInArms.text: Every ten turns, each city with an Armoury raises the best melee unit you can build. They cost no upkeep.

dominionCircumvallation.name: Circumvallation
dominionCircumvallation.flavor: A wall facing in, and a wall facing out.
dominionCircumvallation.text: While a rival city is under siege with at least one of your units beside it, it adds no production toward a Magnum Opus. You can see which rival cities are raising one.
deferred: Stopping a rival town's work on the great work, and seeing which rival towns are raising one, both need changes the game does not have yet.

dominionTheGrandCoalition.name: The Grand Coalition
dominionTheGrandCoalition.flavor: Old enemies march together against the one who would end the age.
dominionTheGrandCoalition.text: While at war with an empire raising a Magnum Opus, your military units gain +6 strength against it, and cities with a Barracks produce military units 30% faster.

dominionTheProconsuls.name: The Proconsuls
dominionTheProconsuls.flavor: A governor with a legion behind him needs no other argument.
dominionTheProconsuls.text: Captured cities with a garrison cost no authority and gain +10 defence.

dominionTheGrandCampaign.name: Commission: The Grand Campaign
dominionTheGrandCampaign.flavor: Three cities, one season, one name on every banner.
dominionTheGrandCampaign.text: Commission. Capture three cities while this card is seated. Then gain a great general, and science and culture each equal to ten times those cities' total population. The card leaves its chair.

dominionTheCapturedMarvel.name: Commission: The Captured Marvel
dominionTheCapturedMarvel.flavor: The marvel was theirs to build and ours to keep.
dominionTheCapturedMarvel.text: Commission. Capture a city that holds a world wonder or was another empire's original capital. Then gain science and culture each equal to twenty times its population, plus 200 of each for every world wonder in it. The card leaves its chair.

theVarangianGuard.name: The Varangian Guard
theVarangianGuard.flavor: Foreign axemen sworn to the emperor himself, and the last to leave a field.
theVarangianGuard.text: Elite units may attack twice a turn.

theGreatBombards.name: The Great Bombards
theGreatBombards.flavor: Walls that stood for a thousand years came down in an afternoon.
theGreatBombards.text: Your siege units break a town's walls in one blow.

theHorde.name: The Horde
theHorde.flavor: Where the horde passes, the whole valley burns.
theHorde.text: Pillaging a hex also pillages every enemy improvement beside it.

theHarrying.name: The Harrying
theHarrying.flavor: An unguarded town that watches its fields burn does not stay loyal for long.
theHarrying.text: Pillaging a hex beside a rival town with no garrison throws that town into unrest.

theSteppeConfederacy.name: The Steppe Confederacy
theSteppeConfederacy.flavor: No writ reaches the open steppe, and no border waits for one.
theSteppeConfederacy.text: Negative authority no longer stops your borders growing. While authority is negative, gain +50% production toward mounted units.

theConsularRoads.name: The Consular Roads
theConsularRoads.flavor: The road brings the legion, and the legion brings the law.
theConsularRoads.text: Cities connected to your capital by road and holding a garrison gain +5 science and +5 culture, and are pacified at once.

theUniversalMonarchy.name: The Universal Monarchy
theUniversalMonarchy.flavor: One crown over every people, and every people under one crown.
theUniversalMonarchy.text: Towns you capture cost no authority. Towns you found cost twice as much.
